standard_prerequisites: Definition def (Definition 3.3, line 475) of the operations m_k, the Bott-Morse A-infinity-operation in the de Rham model.
The boundary-orientation formula of Proposition bdryori (Proposition 4.1, line 564), valid under the tree-like K-system and CF-perturbation framework (cited [FOOO20] at line 514, outside the span).

The decomposed (1,0)-case relations: equation (4.1) rel1 (line 528), m_{1,0} circ m_{k,B} = (-1)^{epsilon} d (ev_0^B)_! (ev_1^{B*} xi_1 wedge ... wedge xi_k), and equation (4.2) rel2 (line 534), m_{k,B} circ m-hat_{1,0} = (-1)^{epsilon+1} (ev_0^B)_! d (ev_1^{B*} xi_1 wedge ... wedge xi_k).
The Stokes-type formula of Proposition corrStokes (Proposition 2.5, line 241, whose statement cites [FOOO20, Proposition 27.2] outside the span).
The composition formula of Lemma lemma (Lemma 4.3, line 849) with its sign kappa' (equation (4.5)), for the summands with both factors different from (1,0).
Standing: the graded-coderivation extension m-hat_{k,B}, the shifted degree |.|', and epsilon(xi_1,...,xi_k).
core_obligations: The operations m_k, k = 0,1,..., of Definition def satisfy the filtered A-infinity relation: sum over k'+k''=k+1 of m_{k'} circ m-hat_{k''} (xi_1,...,xi_k) = 0 for k = 1,2,... .
proof_roadmap: Boundary term: by Proposition bdryori (4.1), the summation of the right-hand side of (4.5) over k', k'', B', B'' with k'+k''=k+1, B=B'+B'', (k',B'),(k'',B'') != (1,0) equals (-1)^{kappa+kappa'} (ev_0^B restricted to the boundary of M_{k+1}(B;L;R))_! (ev_1^{B*} xi_1 wedge ... wedge xi_k) (Claim rel3, rendered Claim 4.5, lines 964-968).
Sign alignment: kappa + kappa' is congruent mod 2 to epsilon(xi_1,...,xi_k) + 1 + dim M_{k+1}(B;L;R) + sum_i deg xi_i (align*, lines 971-975).

Stokes input: by Proposition corrStokes (2.5), d (ev_0^B)_! (ev_1^{B*} xi_1 wedge ... wedge xi_k) = (ev_0^B)_! d (ev_1^{B*} xi_1 wedge ... wedge xi_k) + (-1)^nu (ev_0^B restricted to the boundary)_! (ev_1^{B*} xi_1 wedge ... wedge xi_k), where nu = dim M_{k+1}(B;L;R) + sum_i deg xi_i (gather (4.8), lines 978-982).

Assembly: combining (4.1), (4.2), Claim 4.5 and (4.8) - the two (1,0)-pieces contribute the d-terms with signs (-1)^epsilon and (-1)^{epsilon+1} by (4.1)/(4.2), the non-(1,0)-pieces contribute the boundary term with sign (-1)^{kappa+kappa'} by the Claim, and the sign alignment of step 2 (kappa+kappa' congruent to nu + epsilon + ... mod 2) discharges the boundary pieces against the Stokes display - yields the displayed three-term vanish (gather*, lines 986-990) for all (k,B) != (1,0).
Remaining case: for (k,B) = (1,0), m_{1,0} = d and m_{1,0} circ m_{1,0} = d circ d = 0 clearly (line 991). Hence the theorem.
